headline: The New York Times, the news agency Agence France-Presse and The Economist have joined SPUR, a coalition of publishers that wants to stop AI companies using their content without permission.
score_reason: Lowered from the pool score of 6: the joining happened and was first reported on 12 Oct 2026, before today's window, and no AI company is reported to have agreed to the coalition's standards.
importance_line: Publishers and the journalists they employ may gain a stronger hand in demanding payment from AI companies, which matters to AI developers that train on news, but SPUR's standards and systems are still being built and the report does not say any AI company has agreed to use them.
summary: Reuters reports that the New York Times, Agence France-Presse and The Economist joined the Standards for Publisher Usage Rights (SPUR) coalition on Monday 12 Oct 2026; the coalition, launched in February, now has more than 80 members in over 20 countries, including The Atlantic, the Financial Times, the BBC and the Associated Press. SPUR is building standards and technical systems to help publishers track how AI companies use their content and to arrange licensing, and our 3 Oct 2026 edition carried Digiday's report on its tracking standard.
notes: Pool item is CNA's copy of the Reuters wire story; text read at https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/nyt-economist-among-publishers-joining-coalition-curb-unpaid-ai-use-6454436 and the Reuters link was found through Google News (published 12 Oct 2026, 23:06 UTC). Event of 12 Oct is before the 13 Oct window start, so the score is lowered by 1 as instructed; the previous edition (12 Oct) ended at 08:12 UTC so this story fell in the gap between editions and the editor may restore 6.
